The words

'Tis my happiness below
Not to live without the cross,
But the Saviour's power to know,
Sanctifying every loss:
Trials must and will befall;
But with humble faith to see
Love inscribed upon them all, —
This is happiness to me.

God in Israel sows the seeds
Of affliction, pain, and toil;
These spring up, and choke the weeds
Which would else o'erspread the soil;
Trials make our faith sublime,
Trials give new life to prayer,
Lift us to a holier clime,
Make us strong to do and bear.

How to sing it from the solfa

  • Find doh first. Play or hum F and sing d r m f s up from it, so the whole choir has the key in their ears before you start.
  • Pitch the first note. The tune starts on m (A).
  • Count the time. 4/4 means four crotchet beats in each bar. In the grid every cell is half a crotchet: a dash (–) holds the note before it, and _ is a rest.
  • Know the notes. The tune uses d r m f s l t. A comma after a note (s,) is the octave below; an apostrophe (d') is the octave above.

About the hymn

William Cowper wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 271, “The Cross”. The compilers changed some of the words, and this is their version.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens Double (7.7.7.7 D) (7.7.7.7.7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MESSIAH (HERALD); any other Sevens Double (7.7.7.7 D) tune fits them as well.

  • Words: William Cowper (1731–1800)
  • Music (1839): Louis J. F. Herold (died undefined)
  • Arranged (1839): George Kingsley (died undefined)

Questions about 'Tis My Happiness Below

What is the doh of 'Tis My Happiness Below?

In this version, in F major, doh is F. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does 'Tis My Happiness Below start on?

It starts on m (A in F major). Find doh first, then sing up or down to m.

Is 'Tis My Happiness Below in the public domain?

Yes. William Cowper died in 1800, Louis J. F. Herold died in undefined, George Kingsley died in undefined; the words were in print by 1848 and the music in 1839. Everyone named died before 1955 and both were published before 1929, so the hymn is out of copyright in the UK, the EU, the United States and Nigeria. Modern arrangements and translations can still be under copyright.
